topics.topic: Backup authenticated-encryption construction, envelope, metadata authentication, and key interpretation
questions: Which authenticated-encryption algorithm, nonce-generation rule, file envelope, key interpretation and authentication-failure behavior implement this guarantee?
Must a backup detect alteration of its encrypted contents and readable metadata before decryption or retention decisions, and what fixed cryptographic construction provides that guarantee?
Which authenticated-encryption algorithm, nonce generation, key interpretation or derivation, metadata authentication and key-digest algorithm make these guarantees verifiable?

judgement.why: This is the same unchanged question about backup authenticated encryption, envelope metadata and key interpretation already assigned to State 6.

precedent.topic: Required backup encryption, integrity, metadata, and key-digest format
quotes: Each backup is encrypted with the backup key the configuration holds at its making (A17).
A backup cannot be read without the key it was made with.
precedent.why: The algorithm, nonce, authenticated envelope, key identifier and cryptographic-version representation are encoding and file-format contract details owned by State 6.

topics.topic: Deterministic precedence of startup configuration checks and diagnostics
questions: What is the total check order within each numbered rule and between rule 1's exact-item requirement and rule 5's missing, malformed and unknown-item checks?
What is the total check order when several configuration defects exist, and therefore which failed item must the diagnostic name?
What is the order among multiple items checked inside the same rule, such as the four token lengths, pairwise secret equality checks, unknown items and multiple path failures?

quotes: The checks run in the order of these rules and the first that fails stops the start; a new store is made only after every other check has passed, and a failed start leaves no file it made.
Registry checks the configuration when it starts and serves nothing until every check passes; a failed check stops the start with a diagnostic that names the failed item and never its value (R0-37).
judgement.divergence: One implementation checks items and subchecks in a fixed documented order and always diagnoses the first by that order; another iterates tokens, secrets or paths in storage-dependent order and diagnoses a different defect, which the owner notices at startup.
judgement.why: The rules require the first failure to determine the diagnostic but do not order multiple checks within a numbered rule.

topics.topic: Safe recognition and naming of backup, temporary, status, malformed, and unrelated files
questions: How is Registry guaranteed not to delete an unrelated owner file that happens to begin with the temporary prefix, and how are temporary, kept and status names made disjoint?
At startup, scheduling, retention cleanup and status reconstruction, what happens when an existing kept backup cannot be parsed or no longer passes integrity or authentication checks?
What happens when a file under the kept-backup prefix has unreadable, malformed or unauthenticated metadata: does it count as a kept backup, block a run, get deleted, or get ignored?

quotes: A backup and its check file are written under temporary names in the backup location — every one beginning with the prefix the release declares for them — and become a kept backup only when complete; at every start and every run Registry first removes every file left there under that prefix, and no other file.

Each run writes its outcome and instant to a status file in the backup location, which a restart keeps; it is written after the backup is kept or the run fails, and a status file missing, unreadable or older than the newest kept backup is rewritten at start from the kept backups, which alone say whether a day has one; the owner interface shows the newest kept backup's instant and that last outcome, so the owner sees when a backup holds the import (A16 rule 10).
A backup that fails the check is deleted and counts as failed.
judgement.divergence: One implementation treats every prefix-matching file as Registry-owned and deletes or counts it despite malformed metadata; another ignores, quarantines or blocks on an unrecognizable file, which the owner notices through deleted files, startup or backup-run behavior, status reconstruction and retention.
judgement.why: The texts prescribe prefix deletion and reconstruction from kept backups but do not define ownership-safe naming or behavior for an existing kept-looking file that is malformed or later corrupted.

topics.topic: Serialization policy and ordering for concurrent owner-session requests
questions: When two such requests arrive concurrently, what determines their serial order, especially for upload versus confirmation, confirmation versus confirmation, and sign-out versus another session-changing request?

Are all requests carrying an owner session serialized because all update `last_request`, or may ordinary reads run concurrently while only confirmation, upload, submission and sign-out transitions are serialized?
Which serial order applies to concurrent uploads, confirmation displays, submissions and sign-out requests when different orders produce different accepted actions?

quotes: The requests of one owner session that change its state — showing a confirmation step, uploading a file, a submission — are applied one at a time: each sees the session as the one before left it, so a confirmation bound to a file a later upload replaced is refused (A16 rule 2).

An owner request is any request to the owner interface that carries the valid session, whatever its answer; its arrival restarts the 30 minutes — of concurrent requests the latest arrival counts; before the first request it runs from the sign-in.
A sign-out is applied in turn with the session's other requests that change it: one admitted before it completes its change to the store, and leaves nothing in the ended session.
judgement.divergence: One implementation serializes concurrent session mutations by arrival order while another uses transaction-acquisition or completion order, so different uploads, confirmations or submissions survive or succeed and the owner notices; implementations may also serialize all requests or allow reads to run concurrently because updating last_request is not classified.
judgement.why: The rules demand serialization but do not define its ordering key or whether the last-request update makes every owner request a serialized session mutation.

topics.topic: Byte encoding and normalization of textual secrets and keys
questions: How are configured textual values converted to bytes for length, equality, authentication and constant-time comparison, and is any Unicode, whitespace or encoding normalization applied?
Which byte representation is used for length, equality and constant-time comparison when configuration supplies textual credentials or an encoded backup key?

judgement.why: This is the same unchanged question about configured-secret encoding, normalization, equality and byte-length measurement already assigned to State 6.

quotes:
A secret — each token, the owner credential and the backup key — is at
   least 32 bytes long; a shorter one fails the start.

A presented secret is compared in constant time; no secret enters a record,
   a log line, an audit entry, a diagnostic or an answer (R0-23, R0-37).
precedent.why: The textual or binary representation, decoding, equality and byte-counting rules for credential fields are encoding and contract details owned by State 6.

topics.topic: Canonical confirmation-binding encoding and digest algorithm
questions: Which digest algorithm, value encoding, field order, treatment of absent values and collection ordering define the confirmation binding?
How are action, target, revision or access version and inputs encoded without ambiguity and which digest algorithm determines whether submitted inputs equal the confirmed inputs?

judgement.why: This is the same unchanged question about canonical confirmation-input encoding, ordering and digest construction already assigned to State 6.

precedent.topic: Canonical encoding, ordering, and digest algorithm for confirmation-bound inputs
quotes:
kept as a digest of those values in a fixed order, never
   as the values themselves; a submission's inputs are bound when their digest
   equals it.
precedent.why: The canonical byte encoding, field order, digest algorithm and representation of absent values are encoding and contract details owned by State 6.

topics.topic: Catch-up semantics after missed daily backup times
questions: If Registry misses 03:00 on one day and next starts on a later UTC day, is the missed day's run made, is only the current day's backup made, and can a start before the current day's 03:00 create that day's ordinary backup?
On startup after one or more missed 03:00 runs, is one catch-up backup made immediately, which UTC day does it count for, and is the normal 03:00 run later that same day still due?

quotes: A run that 03:00 found Registry stopped is made when it next starts with its service tokens, if no backup was made that UTC day; an owner-only start makes no run (rule 10).

Besides it, at most one backup is made per UTC day, the kept backups themselves saying which days have one, and runs never overlap: a run that falls due while another runs waits for it, and both are made.
judgement.divergence: After several stopped days, one implementation makes one immediate backup attributed to the current day and may skip that day's later 03:00 run, while another attempts a missed-day catch-up or makes both catch-up and current-day runs; the owner notices different backup dates, counts and recovery points.
judgement.why: The phrase “that UTC day” and the interaction between catch-up and the current day's scheduled run are not defined.

topics.topic: Durable scheduling and retry semantics for the required post-import backup
questions: If the immediate post-import backup fails, is the retry still a distinct post-import backup, can an ordinary daily backup satisfy it, and when are both due if the next run is the daily run?

If Registry stops or crashes after the import transaction commits but before the post-import backup run starts or records an outcome, how does the next start know that the extra post-import backup is still due?

quotes: right after it — or, in an owner-only start, at the next start with the tokens (A18 rule 10) — Registry makes a backup run outside the daily schedule (A18), so the import reaches a checked backup as soon as it can, and the owner interface shows when it has (A18 rule 1); a failed run is retried at the next run, and the import stays accepted.
The run after an accepted import (A16) is made even when the day already has a backup, and keeps both; it is not that day's ordinary backup, which is still made at 03:00 or at the next start.
An owner-only start (A17 rule 1) serves the owner interface alone and makes no backup run; a post-import run due then is made at the next start with the service tokens (A16 rule 10).
judgement.divergence: One implementation durably derives or records that the post-import backup remains due and retries it as a distinct extra backup after failure or restart; another loses that obligation after a crash or treats the next ordinary backup as satisfying it, which the owner notices and which changes available restore points.
judgement.why: The texts require a distinct post-import run and retry but do not say how its pending status survives a crash or whether an ordinary run can discharge it.

topics.topic: Exact import-file bytes, digest algorithm, and collision handling
questions: What exact bytes and digest algorithm identify the uploaded file, and how is a digest collision handled?
What exact digest identifies an import file, and are the original uploaded bytes or a parsed/canonicalized representation digested?

judgement.why: This is the same unchanged question about the exact import bytes, digest algorithm and digest representation already assigned to State 6.

precedent.topic: Exact digest and byte representation identifying an import file
quotes: The mapping names the file by its digest.
What Registry defines is the file it accepts on import; its format belongs to States 5 and 6.
precedent.why: The digest algorithm, canonical byte representation and encoded digest form are format and contract details owned by State 6.

topics.topic: Import-upload storage and cleanup guarantees
questions: May the personal-data file be written to a temporary filesystem file, or must it remain in memory, and what deletion, permissions and crash-cleanup guarantees does “dropped” require?

May the uploaded personal-data file be spooled to disk, and what cleanup guarantee applies on replacement, acceptance, sign-out, expiry, restart or process failure so that it does not survive its owner session?

quotes: The uploaded file is kept in the owner session that uploaded it, never in the store, until the import is accepted, another file is uploaded in that session, or the session ends (M11); then it is dropped.
Everything in it ends with the session.
Temporary runtime state; never a durable record beyond its life.
judgement.divergence: One implementation retains the upload only in memory and it disappears on termination; another spools it to disk and may leave personal data after replacement, session expiry or a crash unless later cleanup succeeds, which the owner, host administrator or a party reading the disk notices.
judgement.why: The texts require the upload to end with the session but do not decide whether disk spooling is permitted or define crash-safe deletion and restart cleanup behavior.

topics.topic: Imported-record containment and referential-integrity rules
questions: Which references must each imported record contain, which referenced records must exist, and when is a referring room or pointer included in or excluded from a picked project's import?

If a room or pointer is structurally contained under a picked project but names a different or absent project, is it ignored as belonging to an unpicked project or does it make the picked project malformed?
Which imported record kinds are allowed to name a room, given that State 1's imported Project, Room and ArtifactPointer facts define no room reference except a Room's own identity?

quotes: Registry checks what the picks bring in — each picked project with the rooms and pointers that name it and the v1 value it names — and nothing else of the file; a room or pointer naming another project belongs to that project: records only of projects the owner did not pick are neither checked, shown as conflicts nor imported, and take no part in the duplicate-id check.
A picked project whose room names a project absent from the file refuses the import as malformed.
judgement.why: The first passage excludes a room naming another project from the picked project's checked records, while the required test treats such a room naming an absent project as part of the pick and requires refusal.

topics.topic: Namespace treated as Registry configuration for unknown-item validation
questions: What source or namespace counts as Registry's configuration for the unknown-item check—an isolated Registry file/object, all environment variables, or only variables with a Registry prefix?
What input namespace is parsed as Registry configuration, and do unrelated environment variables count as unknown items that stop startup?

judgement.why: This is the same unchanged question about the configuration source and namespace subject to unknown-item validation already assigned to State 6.

precedent.topic: Configuration source and namespace subject to unknown-item validation
quotes:
The configuration holds exactly these items and no other: the store's
   location; the backup location and the backup key (A18); the owner
   credential; one service token for each service of A09 — PresuPro, Client
   Portal, Cabinet, Cabinet Kernel (R0-20, R0-23) — or, for an owner-only
   start, none of the four: Registry then serves the owner interface alone
   and refuses every service call (A18 rule 10).

A missing, malformed or unknown item fails the start; Registry applies no
   default to any item.
precedent.why: The configuration document, namespace and distinction between its fields and unrelated environment variables are schema and encoding contract details owned by State 6.

topics.topic: Ordering and deduplication of concurrently triggered backup runs
questions: If two ordinary triggers for the same UTC day overlap, must the second be deduplicated or must both backups be made?
When the ordinary daily run and the post-import run become due concurrently, which runs first and which store snapshot is each required to contain?

quotes: Besides it, at most one backup is made per UTC day, the kept backups themselves saying which days have one, and runs never overlap: a run that falls due while another runs waits for it, and both are made.
The run after an accepted import (A16) is made even when the day already has a backup, and keeps both; it is not that day's ordinary backup, which is still made at 03:00 or at the next start.
Every phase runs even when an earlier one failed, but a failed removal skips the new backup.
judgement.divergence: One implementation deduplicates a second concurrent ordinary trigger after the first backup is kept, while another queues both under the “both are made” rule; when an ordinary and post-import run coincide, implementations may run either first, producing different snapshots and metadata that the owner notices during restore or inspection.
judgement.why: The rules do not distinguish duplicate ordinary triggers from distinct due runs or specify the serialization order between ordinary and post-import runs.

topics.topic: Startup behavior when probe or partial-store cleanup fails
questions: What must Registry do if the probe file is created but its removal fails, or if creation of a new store leaves a partial file that cannot be removed?
What must Registry do when its startup probe file is created but cannot be removed?

quotes: The backup location must exist and let Registry create and remove a file in it; otherwise the start fails.
The checks run in the order of these rules and the first that fails stops the start; a new store is made only after every other check has passed, and a failed start leaves no file it made.
judgement.why: If Registry creates the probe file but cannot remove it, the first passage requires startup failure while the second simultaneously requires the failed start to leave no file it made, which Registry cannot guarantee.

topics.topic: Backup-key identifier digest and collision handling
questions: Which digest or keyed identifier is recorded, over which exact key bytes, and how are collisions between key identifiers handled?

topics.topic: Continuation and outcome reporting after retention deletion failures
questions: If deleting one expired backup fails, does Registry continue attempting the other expired backups during that run, and how are multiple failures represented in the outcome?

topics.topic: Effect of an identical replacement upload on pending confirmation
questions: Does uploading byte-for-byte identical content with the same digest invalidate a pending confirmation for the previous upload?

topics.topic: Effect of partial backup-run failures on retention guarantees
questions: Does a failed backup phase lengthen erasure retention when the deletion phase succeeds, and does a failure only in status writing lengthen either guarantee?

topics.topic: Handling collisions in generated owner-session identities
questions: What must Registry do if a newly generated owner-session identity equals an identity of an existing live session?

topics.topic: Meaning of import acceptance after restore
questions: Does “accepts” mean only that the one-time closure check is open, with all A16 authentication, confirmation, malformed-record and conflict checks still applying, or does it promise that the import succeeds?

topics.topic: Owner-session cookie scope, attributes, and Secure behavior
questions: What exact cookie scope and attributes implement “Registry's own origin”, given that cookies are scoped by host/domain and path, not by origin or port, and must the cookie carry Secure on host-local HTTP access?

topics.topic: Recovery of a committed import's old-to-new customer mapping after response loss
questions: How can the owner recover the old-to-new Customer mapping if the transaction commits but its answer is lost, since retry is refused and the closure stores only the file digest?

topics.topic: Representation of intentional owner-only token configuration
questions: How is an intentional owner-only start distinguished from an accidentally missing set of all four token items, and are absent, null and blank token entries equivalent?

topics.topic: Retention and selection of old backup keys after rotation
questions: Where must old backup keys remain available, for how long, and how does the owner select the correct old key when restoring a retained backup?

topics.topic: Sampling and consistency of timestamps produced by one action
questions: When is “now” sampled for an accepted transaction, and must the record's last-changed instant, archived/restricted/ended instant and audit-entry instant produced by one action be exactly the same value?

topics.topic: Serialization order for concurrent sign-in attempts
questions: In what order are concurrent sign-ins applied when their order changes the result, such as a correct credential racing the fifth refused credential?

topics.topic: Short-circuit versus aggregate evaluation of A04 stage-1 checks
questions: When an earlier stage-1 prerequisite fails, must Registry skip dependent checks such as CSRF or confirmation, or evaluate and report every nominal stage-1 failure?

topics.topic: Stage and precedence for validating confirmation fields and binding
questions: At which check are the confirmation's action, target, revision or access version, input digest and age validated, and which failure wins when more than one of them is wrong?
Does stage 1 check only that a matching, unexpired confirmation value exists, or also its binding to the target, inputs and revision, which A04 otherwise assigns to later stages?

topics.topic: Stage and reporting behavior for projects outside an agent session's set
questions: At which stage is a project outside an agent session's set refused, and can any stage 3–5 failure ever be evaluated or reported with it?

topics.topic: Stage classification of malformed identities versus missing records
questions: When a supplied identity cannot be parsed or violates its value format, is it refused as an invalid value at stage 4 or treated as a non-existent record at stage 3, which is ordered first?

topics.topic: Treatment of backups from an abandoned store history after restore
questions: After restoring an older store while the backup location still contains backups from the abandoned later history, do those later backups count for scheduling, status, retention and post-import protection, or must Registry distinguish store histories?

topics.topic: Validation and reporting of imported closed-vocabulary values
questions: Must confirmation refuse an invalid object kind, customer kind or other non-status closed-vocabulary value, and at which step is that reported?

topics.topic: Whether accepted import uploads are dropped from one or all owner sessions
questions: Does accepting an import drop uploaded import files from every owner session, or only from the session that confirmed it?

topics.topic: Whether required import values are validated before or after mapping
questions: Is required-value validation applied to the source record or to the mapped result, so can an owner-supplied display name repair a picked project whose source display name is missing or blank?

topics.topic: Whether serving begins before startup cleanup and catch-up backups finish
questions: Does Registry begin serving before, during or only after the startup cleanup and catch-up backup run completes?
